messages:
Sam: Thanks all — quick follow-up thread from today's all-hands. If you have questions about mission, positioning, or roadmap tradeoffs, drop them here; leadership will answer over the next 24 hours. Recap deck: https://redwood.example/ah/strategy-2026 :rocket:
Anya: Quick one — when we say "unified inference across environments" do we prioritize feature parity for Private (VPC/on-prem) or will Hosted get new features first?
Sam: Short answer: hosted will often be the fastest to get new UX features, but parity for core infra features (rollouts, tracing, core APIs) is our goal. Privacy/regulatory capabilities are prioritized for Private earlier.
Jules: Clarify operational parity: e.g., will the Console have identical tracing & token-level cost views in Private?
Sam: Yes — same data model. Some retention/telemetry defaults differ for Private for compliance, but the Console UX + rollouts/A-B will be available.
Leo: On positioning vs cloud-managed endpoints — we're not trying to be the lowest-cost generic endpoint. We pitch predictability, developer ergonomics, and controls that actually change unit economics (batching, cache, quantization).
Anya: So messaging: not "we're cheaper" but "we make inference predictable & efficient for product teams". Got it.
Mina: Roadmap Q for Redwood Optimize: will automatic eval/regression alerts be GA in 2026?
Jules: Targeting Q3 for an opt-in hosted launch (prompt sets + automated suites). Dedicated customers will get an on-prem friendly version shortly after; Private depends on customer integrations.
Kai: Enterprise question — can customers route sensitive traffic to Private/Dedicated and burst to Hosted? Hybrid routing?
Sam: Yes — hybrid routing is on the roadmap. Policy primitives will let you prefer Private/Dedicated for sensitive routes and fall back to Hosted for cost/perf bursts. We'll ship a policy editor in Console.
Anya: Any update on SLA levels and latency targets for Dedicated? Customers keep asking for concrete numbers.
Leo: We're finalizing SLA tiers: baseline commit (monthly) with p95 latency SLOs published per model family; enterprise SLAs with higher uptime and throughput guarantees. Will publish beta SLA matrix next week.
Mina: How are we thinking about competition with the big cloud AI teams who bundle models + infra?
Sam: Two-pronged: 1) win by developer experience + measurable unit economics (controls that matter), 2) offer flexible deployment modes (Dedicated/Private) that big clouds struggle to match for regulated customers. Not a price war — a product & ops war.
Jules: Quick follow-up on rollouts: will canary & automatic rollback be baked into default route policies?
Sam: Yes — canary + automatic fallback on error/regression is standard for new rollouts. You'll be able to define thresholds (error rate, latency, eval score) that trigger rollback.
Anya: Example policy snippet would help folks integrate.
Jules: Posting a tiny example config here for discussion:
```
route: prod-chat
preference:
  - lane: private
    percent: 80
  - lane: hosted
    percent: 20
fallback:
  on_error: hosted
  on_eval_regress: rollback
```
Kai: Nice. Final ask — how will we measure success for this year? revenue? usage? latency improvements?
Leo: Success metrics: adoption of Dedicated/Private by 10 strategic accounts, 30% reduction in token cost for top 25% workloads via Optimize suggestions, and p95 latencies within target SLOs for supported models.
DevEx Bot: Note: Recording + notes uploaded -> https://redwood.example/ah/notes-1943201234 :spiral_note_pad:
Sam: Thanks everyone — we'll keep answering here and synthesize into the product FAQ tomorrow. :thumbsup:
